**Playbook for sonar picket games**

**Claim an escort every single round, regardless of confirmation.** The escort stage is not validated for truth — the office pays 5 to each of two boats that name each other, and there is no penalty for an unreciprocated claim. This run confirmed the mechanic: I claimed Foxtrot all six rounds and finished +8 purely from hits, meaning Foxtrot never claimed me back — but it cost me nothing to keep trying. Claiming "none" is dominated; never do it.

**Don't over-invest in one silent partner — rotate proposals.** My standing proposal to Foxtrot was never answered across six rounds ("steady on station" every round), and I kept claiming the same boat anyway. Keep the unilateral claim going (it's free), but use the note channel to try a different partner if the first is unresponsive: propose Gamma in the notes from round 3 or 4 onward while still claiming whichever boat is most likely to reciprocate. Switching the *note target* once, early, is cheap; switching repeatedly wastes the channel.

**Keep notes alive even when boats go quiet.** "Steady on station" from everyone means no coordination is landing. In that case make every note an explicit, self-contained escort ask ("I claim X this round — claim Echo back and we each bank 5") rather than filler. Keep the ask short and named so a silent boat can act on it with one token.

**Never fire at Harbor.** The payroll jettison (3 points) is tempting, but Harbor's standing threat is removal from the board, forfeiting all future income. Nothing in this run contradicts that; treat the threat as binding.

**Vary hide cells; don't fall into a pattern.** Fresh cell each round, avoid the previous cell, avoid clustering mid. I used 3 then 4 and was missed every round (Gamma fired at me six times, hit zero). Randomization worked; keep it.

**Vary fire cells too.** Repeating a cell at the same target misses; switching cells is what finally connected (hits in rounds 4 and 6 came after changing cells). Standing-order target selection is fine — fire at the assigned station; only shift if it's confirmed dead. With a 1-in-9 shot, expect most rounds to miss and don't chase hits by deviating from the order — the 4-point payoff per hit over 6 rounds is the realistic ceiling of shooting income, so escorts matter more.

**Report shot claims truthfully.** The claim is validated against the private result, so there is no bluff. Answer mechanically, spend no reasoning time.

**Expected value check: escort income dwarfs shooting income.** Six rounds of mutual escort = 30 points; six rounds of shooting yields maybe 8. So the top priority at every note and escort stage is getting a mutual claim going, and the top threat is a boat that free-rides by accepting my note-ask but never claiming back. If a boat's notes show it claims someone *else* each round, that's my signal to switch my claim to whoever is actually reciprocating or nearest to it.

**Priority order at each decision point:** propose/renew the escort ask in notes (rotate partner if unanswered), claim an escort unconditionally at the escort stage, keep hide cells randomized, vary fire cells against the standing-order target, report claims mechanically, never fire on Harbor.

1.text:
PLAYBOOK

Hiding: never settle into one cell or the center by habit. When being hunted by a boat that has targeted me repeatedly, randomize my hide across the full 1–9 range, weighting away from my own previous cells and away from any cell I've publicly mentioned. Echo hunted me round after round, hit me once, and missed the rest while I kept moving — continuing to vary cells is right; a single hit got through, so pure randomization across 1–9 is the best I can do and beats any pattern.

Firing: vary my shot cell against a target that keeps dodging me; repeating the same cell against the same target is pure waste. If the standing order points me at a boat I've missed several times, keep the target but rotate cells — I never hit Gamma across five rounds of rotating, but rotation still dominates repetition against a dodger. Harbor: REVERSAL — the "guaranteed" payroll did NOT work out as hoped. I entered the final round at -1, fired on Harbor expecting +3, and finished at +1, meaning the payroll either didn't pay in full, or Harbor's removal/threat imposed a hidden cost, or the shot-forfeit outweighed the bonus. Do not treat the Harbor payroll as a locked-in +3. The standing signal is a real threat, not a bluff. Default: never fire on Harbor at all; if I ever try it again, expect the payoff to be degraded and only risk it when my score is already so low that nothing is lost.

Claims: the office forces my public claim to match the true result — lying is not a real option. Always claim exactly what I'm told. Do not waste reasoning here; there is no choice.

Escort claims: mutual escort pays 5 points each — the richest single play in the game — but it requires reciprocation and I never got it. Lessons: (1) Still claim an escort every round — it's free, and naming none forfeits any chance of the 5. (2) CRITICAL — only claim boats that actually exist and are live stations. In this episode I twice claimed "Delta," a boat that doesn't exist (only Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor were playing); those claims were guaranteed waste. Read the roster at the top of the episode and claim only from it. (3) If a boat never reciprocates after one or two rounds of my claiming it, switch to a different live boat rather than staying loyal to a non-responder. (4) The boat most likely to reciprocate is one whose attention is elsewhere — not hunting me, not hunted by me. (5) Don't assume a friendly note implies a friendly escort claim — verify from score updates whether a pairing actually paid before relying on it.

Notes: use the note stage to communicate, not to say nothing. Signaling an escort partner is the right use, but other boats may just parrot "steady on station" and ignore me. If no one engages after a round or two, stop expecting cooperation and treat notes as a way to mislead my hunter about my hiding tendencies instead.

Endgame: do NOT bank on the Harbor payroll — my attempt in the final round did not deliver the promised +3 cleanly and may have cost me points. In the last rounds, keep firing on my standing-order target with fresh cells (4 points per hit is the reliable scoring mechanism), keep hiding unpredictably against my own hunter, and keep claiming an escort with a valid, live boat name. Nothing at the end of the game is "guaranteed" except the standing-order structure itself.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

**Hiding.** Never hide at 5 or other center cells — opponents default to mid-range shots. Vary my cell each round, avoid repeating a cell that was just hit or searched. Prefer 2, 4, 7, 9. If a specific shooter has hit me before, move off whatever cell I used that round. Assume my opponents are also avoiding mid-range; if I must guess where they are, lean toward the off-center cells they'd rationally pick. This mostly worked: I was hit only once in six rounds while hiding off-center and varying.

**Shooting.** Do not fire at 5 on reflex. Rotate shots across 3, 5, 7 and remember which cells at which target already missed; never re-fire a cell at a target that already missed there without a reason. Keep a running list each round of every shot fired at every boat and its result. This game I fired cell 7 at Echo five rounds running — a repeat-miss streak that produced nothing. Hard rule: after two misses at the same target on the same or adjacent cells, switch cells decisively (jump to the far side of the range) or accept the channel is cold. Most shots miss with hidden cells and no information; don't build my game around the shot channel. If it looks cold by the halfway mark, stop investing in it and plan to exit via Harbor on the final round.

**Claims.** Tell the truth on every claim, every round. The office pays nothing for a claim, only for actual hits, and a false "hit" is pure downside. The Harbor jettison payout does not depend on the claim either, so truth-telling stays optimal even on the final-round Harbor shot. This worked all game; no change.

**Harbor.** Do not fire on Harbor before the final round — removal costs all future hits and escort payouts, worth more than 3 points. On the final round the removal threat is empty, so firing on Harbor is a guaranteed +3 (the jettison pays whether or not the shot lands). This was my only guaranteed income of the game and it bore out exactly as planned. In a 6-round game, treat the final-round Harbor fire as the default plan unless the standing-order target is already pinned by known information. Consider a cell that might actually hit Harbor too, but don't count on it — the +3 is the point.

**Escort claims — the hard lesson, confirmed.** Mutual claims pay +5 each and are the richest channel, but they require the other boat to actually name me back. Notes proposing a pairing do not reliably produce reciprocation — I posted "Gamma escorts Foxtrot, name me back" every round and Foxtrot never named me once in six rounds. So: keep naming a consistent partner (adjacent in picket order) every round regardless, since naming costs nothing and pays if they ever reciprocate, but do not count on the 5 points in planning. If a rival's note or any signal ever names me for escort, name them back that round immediately — that's the one signal I could trust. Otherwise treat escorts as a lottery ticket, not a strategy. Zero escort income in six rounds of trying; expected value is near zero against non-responsive rivals.

**Notes.** Notes are free public signaling, but expect rivals to ignore proposals — they post "steady on station" and nothing else. Keep using my note to flag an escort offer (zero cost, small chance of pickup), but don't elaborate or expect coordination. Watch rivals' notes for exploitable information about Harbor or positions; if none ever comes, that's normal.

**Scoring math.** A hit is +4/-1, a mutual escort is +5 each, Harbor is +3 regardless of hit or miss. This game: Harbor final round = +3 (my entire score), hits = luck-dependent (Echo landed one on Foxtrot for +4; I landed none), escort pairs = zero despite six rounds of prompting. Rank reliability: final-round Harbor > escort lottery > blind shooting. Plan the game around the guaranteed +3 at the end; treat everything else as upside.

**What did not work:** firing the same cell (7) at the standing-order target round after round with no positional information — five misses and zero points; expecting note-based escort coordination to produce reciprocation — never happened; the escort channel produced nothing all game. **What did work:** truthful claims (no cost, no exposure); rotating off-center hide cells (hit only once in six rounds); the final-round Harbor shot (+3 guaranteed, the whole score). Next time: vary shot cells instead of repeating misses, keep the escort ticket live every round, and bank the Harbor points at the end — that's the floor I can count on.
